ei.title: Chapter 1-02 3번: The Exciting Atmosphere of a Football Game
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: More than a thousand people showed up at the field to cheer for the hometown high school football team. There was a long line at the ticket booth that stretched down the street. The delicious smell of popcorn and hot dogs was everywhere, and the refreshment stand ran out of food before halftime. Everyone was cheering: the crowd waving flags, the cheerleaders, the band playing loud music, the players, the officials, the parents running the hot dog stand, the policeman, even me! The cheerleaders were whistling and stomping their feet on the aluminum bleachers, making a loud noise. The cheerleaders looked up in delighted surprise. For the first time, they were hearing something come back from the stands — a huge cheer! They did cartwheels and backflips and even a three-tier pyramid. The old-timers said it was the loudest, most exciting game they'd ever been to.

questions.passage: More than a thousand people showed up at the field to (A)[cheer / jeer] for the hometown high school football team. There was a (B)[long / short] line at the ticket booth that stretched down the street. The (C)[bland / delicious] smell of popcorn and hot dogs was everywhere, and the refreshment stand ran out of food before halftime. Everyone was cheering: the crowd waving flags, the cheerleaders, the band playing loud music, the players, the officials, the parents running the hot dog stand, the policeman, even me! The cheerleaders were whistling and stomping their feet on the aluminum bleachers, making a loud noise. The cheerleaders looked up in delighted surprise. For the first time, they were hearing something come back from the stands — a huge cheer! They did cartwheels and backflips and even a three-tier pyramid. The old-timers said it was the loudest, most exciting game they'd ever been to.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 고향 팀을 응원하러(cheer) 나왔고, 매표소에 긴(long) 줄이 있었으며, 맛있는(delicious) 냄새가 가득했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① cheer — short — delicious (B 반대: 긴→짧은)
✅ ② cheer — long — delicious — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ jeer — long — delicious (A 반대: 응원하다→야유하다)
❌ ④ cheer — long — bland (C 반대: 맛있는→싱거운)

questions.passage: More than a thousand people showed up at the field to cheer for the hometown high school football team. There was a long line at the ticket booth that stretched down the street. The delicious smell of popcorn and hot dogs was everywhere, and the refreshment stand ran out of food before halftime. Everyone was cheering: the crowd (A)[folding / waving] flags, the cheerleaders, the band playing (B)[loud / quiet] music, the players, the officials, the parents running the hot dog stand, the policeman, even me! The cheerleaders were whistling and stomping their feet on the aluminum bleachers, making a loud noise. The cheerleaders looked up in (C)[dismayed / delighted] surprise. For the first time, they were hearing something come back from the stands — a huge cheer! They did cartwheels and backflips and even a three-tier pyramid. The old-timers said it was the loudest, most exciting game they'd ever been to.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 군중이 깃발을 흔들며(waving), 밴드가 시끄러운(loud) 음악을 연주했고, 치어리더들이 기쁜(delighted) 놀라움으로 올려다봤다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① waving — quiet — delighted (B 반대: 시끄러운→조용한)
❌ ② waving — loud — dismayed (C 반대: 기쁜→실망한)
❌ ③ folding — loud — delighted (A 반대: 흔드는→접는)
✅ ④ waving — loud — delighted — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: More than a thousand people showed up at the field to cheer for the hometown high school football team. There was a long line at the ticket booth that stretched down the street. The delicious smell of popcorn and hot dogs was everywhere, and the refreshment stand ran out of food before halftime. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 치어리더들이 발을 구르며(stomping) 시끄러운 소리를 냈고, 관중석에서 엄청난(huge) 환호가 돌아왔으며, 가장 신나는(exciting) 경기였다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① stomping — huge — exciting — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② tiptoing — huge — exciting (A 반대: 발을 구르다→살금살금 걷다)
❌ ③ stomping — tiny — exciting (B 반대: 엄청난→작은)
❌ ④ stomping — huge — dull (C 반대: 신나는→지루한)
det.tip: stomping(발을 구르다) ↔ tiptoing(살금살금 걷다), huge(엄청난) ↔ tiny(작은)

det.korean: '조용한(silent)'이 아니라 '시끄러운(loud)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 알루미늄 관람석을 발로 굴러서 큰 소리를 냈다.

③ surprise — 놀라움, 원문 일치

det.korean: 간식 매점이 하프타임 전에 '음식이 다 떨어졌다(ran out of food)'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① playing loud music — 시끄러운 음악 연주 (밴드 행위, 매점과 무관)
❌ ② waving flags — 깃발 흔들기 (군중 행위, 매점과 무관)
✅ ③ ran out of food — 음식이 다 떨어지다 ←정답
❌ ④ stomping their feet — 발 구르기 (치어리더 행위, 매점과 무관)
det.tip: run out of = 다 써버리다, 떨어지다

questions.passage: More than a thousand people showed up at the field to cheer for the hometown high school football team. There was a long line at the ticket booth that stretched down the street. The delicious smell of popcorn and hot dogs was everywhere, and the refreshment stand ran out of food before halftime. Everyone was cheering: the crowd waving flags, the cheerleaders, the band playing loud music, the players, the officials, the parents running the hot dog stand, the policeman, even me! The cheerleaders were whistling and stomping their feet on the aluminum bleachers, making a loud noise. The cheerleaders looked up in delighted surprise. For the first time, they were hearing something come back from the stands — a huge cheer! They did __________ and even a three-tier pyramid. The old-timers said it was the loudest, most exciting game they'd ever been to.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 치어리더들은 '옆돌기와 백플립(cartwheels and backflips)'과 삼단 피라미드까지 했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the aluminum bleachers — 알루미늄 관람석 (앞 문장 맥락)
❌ ② the ticket booth — 매표소 (도입부 맥락)
❌ ③ the hot dog stand — 핫도그 판매대 (중간부 맥락)
✅ ④ cartwheels and backflips — 옆돌기와 백플립 ←정답
